title: 224. stop ‘shoulding’ + shaming yourself
description_html:
in this week’s solo episode, i open up about the mental health struggle i’ve recently been having and how i’ve developed a ‘should’ mentality around it. i explain how when we constantly tell ourselves we ‘should’ be a certain way with our mental health, we’re actually creating shame and stopping ourselves from living our best lives.

in this episode, i break down how we can all stop ‘shoulding’ and shaming ourselves and instead create actionable changes in our lives.
talk_about: how i caught myself using a ‘should’ mentality
self-shame + how it gets in the way of our goals
the psychology behind why we experience shame
DBT skills to use when we’re feeling shame
taking accountability when we’re acting out of shame
guilt vs. shame + why that difference matters
forgiving ourselves for what’s causing us shame

summary: sadie opens up about her ongoing struggle with sleep and how she caught herself in a harmful 'should' mentality—believing she should be able to maintain a consistent sleep schedule without extra support, even though resources and scaffolding are available to her. she unpacks the psychology of shame versus guilt, explains how shame can block us from accepting help and reaching our goals, and shares dbt skills for recognizing when shame doesn't fit the facts. the episode walks through opposite action techniques, the importance of self-forgiveness, and how to stop getting in our own way when we need support.
quote: guilt is I did something wrong. shame is I am wrong.
quote_display: GUILT is i did something wrong. SHAME is i am wrong.
